headline.title: Pre-season: cold nights ahead.
headline.text: All 19 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in White Mountains and Northern Vermont. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

camelback.headline: Freeze Warning issued October 17 at 2:10AM EDT until October 18 at 9:00AM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
camelback.text: * WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures as low as 30 expected. * WHERE...In New Jersey, Sussex County. In Pennsylvania, Carbon and Monroe Counties. * WHEN...From 1 AM to 9 AM EDT Sunday. * IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor plumbing.

sevensprings.headline: Freeze Warning issued October 17 at 1:07AM EDT until October 18 at 9:00AM EDT by NWS State College PA
sevensprings.text: * WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures between 25 and 30 expected. * WHERE...Most of central Pennsylvania. * WHEN...From 1 AM to 9 AM EDT Sunday. * IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor plumbing. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Valley locations and sheltered rural areas will experience the coldest temperatures.

snowshoe.headline: Freeze Warning issued October 17 at 12:35AM EDT until October 18 at 9:00AM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
snowshoe.text: * WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures as low as 29 expected. * WHERE...Portions of northeast Kentucky, southeast Ohio, southwest Virginia, and central, northeast, northern, southeast, southern, and western West Virginia. * WHEN...From 1 AM to 9 AM EDT Sunday. * IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor plumbing.

BTV.excerpt:
Snowfall is expected for portions of the mountains above 1500-2000 feet this morning, then widespread gusty winds and cold temperatures continue today before a moderating trend begins early next week.
The long term is very quiet with comfortable temperatures and dry conditions prevailing for the upcoming week.

ALY.excerpt:
) Continued gusty winds and unseasonably chilly conditions today. A coating to a few tenths of an inch of snow are possible in the higher terrain through this morning.
) Dry weather with temperatures moderating to near seasonable levels late Sunday into early next week.

GYX.excerpt:
A seasonably cold airmass and gusty winds arrive behind the cold front to start the weekend, with wintry conditions across the higher terrain.
Mild and dry conditions look to persist from Sunday through much of next week as high pressure dominates over the Northeast.

BUF.excerpt:
) Chilly through Sunday morning with a few lingering rain and wet snow showers across higher terrain this morning.
) An extended period of dry and warmer weather begins Sunday afternoon and likely lasts through next weekend.

PHI.excerpt:
A cold airmass builds into the region this weekend. Freeze Warnings are in effect for tonight. Another round of frost is possible Sunday night into Monday morning.
Uncertainty persists regarding a nor'easter developing off the coast of the southern Mid-Atlantic that may cause unsettled conditions and hazardous marine impacts early next week.

CTP.excerpt:
) Frost/Freeze late tonight into early Sunday morning
) Extended stretch of dry weather next week

RLX.excerpt:
) Widespread frost/freeze conditions are expected tonight into early Sunday morning.
) Quiet weather and a warming trend are expected next week.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Dry, with cold nights.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:20}} to {{t:46}}, with up to {{s:0.5}} of snow.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 25).

NWS Burlington forecasters, Saturday 3:14 AM: "Snowfall is expected for portions of the mountains above 1500-2000 feet this morning, then widespread gusty winds and cold temperatures continue today before a moderating trend begins early next week."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans warmer than normal and slightly drier than normal.
